gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The director, ___ we met at the conference, has written to us.
gaps.hint: person as object, but the clause is non-defining
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses 'that' cannot replace 'who', even when the person is the object.

gaps.sentence: The tool with ___ I fixed the shelf is in the garage.
gaps.explanation: 'With which' is required after the preposition; relative 'that' cannot follow a preposition.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The festival, during ___ the town is full of visitors, takes place in July.
gaps.hint: preposition + event in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'During which' is the formal pattern; 'during when' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: There are cases ___ this rule simply does not apply.
gaps.explanation: 'Cases where ...' means 'cases in which ...'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause without a subject.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ he resigned was never explained.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' is the fixed pattern.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.
